measured.heard: The program stores 66 in the int A. Is an int 4 bytes on this machine. 66 fits in its low byte. 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 0, which is hex 42. Percent D formats an int as a signed decimal number. So for a equals 66 it gives 66. The cast to unsigned converts 66 to unsigned int. 66 is representable there. So the value stays 66 and percent U gives 66. What do you predict? Commit to an answer before the answer comes. The cast to double converts the value 66 to the double 66.0. On this machine that doubles bits are not the bits of a. Percent F prints a finite double with six digits after the decimal point when no precision is given. So it prints 66 followed by a point and six zeroes. Percent C converts the int 66 to unsigned car and writes that character. In ASCII code 66 is B. Print F does not reinterpret the bits of a for percent F. It receives the double that the cast to double made. On this machine the last line prints that doubles own bits in hex. They are not the bits of a. Without the cast, printf gets the int aware percent F needs a double and the behavior is undefined. So U B dot C is compiled for its warning and never run.
